, while the X MAS package can be used to simulate Chandra observations of simulated galaxy clusters, the comparison between the simulated and the input data is not straightforward, especially when dealing with the spectroscopic temperature of the cluster.
X MAS can be used to simulate X ray images of galaxy clusters and to perform a realistic analysis of the simulated data.

X ray observations of clusters are able to probe the cluster thermal structure only on scales of the order of 1 Mpc, while smaller scale substructures are washed out by the sky background and instrumental resolution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, to make a meaningful comparison between simulations and observations, the analysis of simulated data should be performed in the same way of real observations.
X ray observations can be simulated with a high degree of fidelity.

X MAS can be used to simulate Chandra ACIS observations, and it can be used as an important tool to interpret the results of hydro N body simulations in a way which is directly comparable to observations.
